patterns.label: am / is / are + wearing
examples: I am not wearing a coat.
patterns.rule: I takes am; he, she and it take is; you, we and they take are.

patterns.label: Are you wearing...? / Is he wearing...?
examples: Are you wearing gloves? Yes, I am. No, I am not.
Is he wearing a coat? Yes, he is. No, he isn't.
Is she wearing boots? Yes, she is.
patterns.rule: Questions swap the subject and the be-verb.

patterns.label: So am I / Neither am I
examples: I am wearing a hat. - So am I.
I am not wearing socks. - Neither am I.
She is wearing a scarf. - So is he.
patterns.rule: Agree with a positive statement using So am I; agree with a negative statement using Neither am I.

core.why: You takes are, even for one person.
The boys = they, so use are.
Questions about she start with Is.
You pairs with are, even in questions.

core.sentence: I am wearing a t-shirt. She ___ wearing a sweater.
core.why: She takes is, even in a contrast sentence.

challenging.sentence: Ben and Leo ___ wearing jackets, and Mia ___ wearing a hat.
challenging.why: Two people take are; one person takes is.

challenging.sentence: I am not wearing socks. - ___ am I.
challenging.why: A negative statement is agreed with Neither am I.

challenging.sentence: I am wearing a scarf. - So ___ I.
challenging.why: So echoes the be-verb, which is am here.
Your brother = he, so use Is.

challenging.sentence: She is wearing a hat, but she ___ wearing gloves.
challenging.why: She takes isn't; amn't and aren't are not correct with she.
Your friends = they, so use are.

easy.text: Dear diary, today is picture day at school. I am wearing a blue shirt and grey pants. My sister is wearing a red dress. She likes her dress very much. My friend Ben is wearing his favourite hat. It is green. We are all happy.

options: A blue shirt and grey pants
questions.answer: A blue shirt and grey pants

core.text: Dear diary, today is picture day at school, so everyone is wearing their best clothes. I am wearing a blue shirt and grey pants, and my shoes are new. My sister is wearing a red dress because red is her favourite colour. My friend Ben is wearing his favourite hat. It is green and very big. Ben says hats make you smart. My teacher is wearing a purple scarf and brown boots. She says we are all looking great, and I think she is right.

questions.q: Why is everyone wearing their best clothes?
Why is the writer's sister wearing a red dress?

options: A purple scarf and brown boots
questions.answer: A purple scarf and brown boots

challenging.text: Dear diary, today is picture day at school, so everyone is wearing their best clothes. I am wearing a blue shirt, grey pants and my new shoes, which are still a little tight. My sister is wearing a red dress because red is her favourite colour; she says a red dress makes a picture perfect. My friend Ben is wearing his favourite hat. It is green and far too big, but Ben says hats make you smart, and nobody can change his mind. Our teacher is wearing a purple scarf and brown boots, and she is not wearing her usual jacket. She says we are all looking great. I look at my sister and I look at Ben, and I think our picture is going to be very funny.

questions.q: How do the writer's new shoes feel?
What does Ben believe about hats?
What is the teacher NOT wearing?
Why does the writer think the picture will be funny?
options: Ben's hat is far too big
questions.answer: Ben's hat is far too big

easy.text: In many countries, students wear a uniform. A uniform is the same clothes for all students. In Japan, many students wear a dark jacket and a hat. In England, many students wear a tie. In some schools, students wear any clothes they like. They are wearing t-shirts and shorts.

options: The same clothes for all students
questions.answer: The same clothes for all students

questions.q: What do many students in England wear?

core.text: In many countries, students wear a uniform. A uniform is the same clothes for all students in one school. In Japan, many students are wearing dark jackets and hats. In England, many students are wearing ties with white shirts. In Australia, some students are wearing shorts because it is very hot there. But not every school has a uniform. In some schools, students are wearing any clothes they like, and every day is different.

questions.q: Why are students in Australia wearing shorts?
What are students in Japan wearing?
What are students wearing in schools without a uniform?

challenging.text: In many countries, students wear a uniform, which is the same clothes for every student in one school. In Japan, many students are wearing dark jackets and hats, even in summer. In England, many students are wearing ties with white shirts, and some of them say the tie is uncomfortable. In Australia, some students are wearing shorts and a light shirt because the sun is very strong there. Uniforms are not the same everywhere, and that is what makes them interesting. But not every school has a uniform. In some schools, students are wearing any clothes they like. Some students say uniforms are a good idea because mornings are easy: you do not think, you just get dressed. Others say clothes show who you are, so a uniform hides your style. What do you think?

questions.q: What are some students in England saying about the tie?
Why are students in Australia wearing a light shirt?
Find a word in the text that means 'hard to wear'.
Why do some students say uniforms are a good idea?
What does the last question ask the reader to do?

tasks.prompt: Listen and repeat: I am wearing a hat.
Listen and repeat: I am not wearing a coat.
Say one true sentence about your clothes. Use: I am wearing ___.
Are you wearing socks? Answer with a full sentence.
Say the clothes chant: Hat and scarf, coat and boots. I am warm from head to boots!

core.model: What are you wearing? I am wearing a green dress. Is your brother wearing a hat? Yes, he is.

tasks.prompt: Ask and answer: What are you wearing? Answer in a full sentence.
Ask and answer: Is your friend wearing a jacket today?
Look at your clothes. Say what you are wearing. Use at least three clothing words.
Your friend says: I am wearing a scarf today. Agree with So am I. Then your friend says: I am not wearing gloves. Agree with Neither am I.
Read the Costume Box dialogue with two voices: you are Mia, then you are Leo.

challenging.model: Today I am wearing my favourite sweater and grey pants. My sister is wearing a dress, and so am I. My brother isn't wearing a coat, and neither am I, because it is warm.

tasks.prompt: Speak for 60 seconds: My Outfit. Say what you are wearing, why you are wearing it, and one thing you agree about with So am I or Neither am I.
Compare two seasons. Say what you are wearing in summer and what you are wearing in winter.
Explain what people wear for rain, snow and sun. Use coat, boots, hat and umbrella.
Answer three follow-up questions in full sentences: What is your favourite piece of clothing? What is your friend wearing today? What do you wear when it is cold?
You are in the Dressing Room. Describe your costume, ask about the weather, and agree twice with So am I or Neither am I.
